main_body: A bare, snow-dusted birch-like tree: a tall pale trunk with dark bark marks, a branching grey/black canopy of twigs with a few snow patches at the top, and a small snow mound at the base.
top_band: none - an organic tree; the vertical column through the trunk runs from branch twigs into a pale trunk with no horizontal top surface. The only horizontal-ish element is a small snow patch at the base.
evidence: The tree is drawn as a flat straight-on silhouette. The trunk is a thin vertical strip about 4-5px wide with dark edge shading, and the branches fan out as a flat 2D pattern. There is no canopy mass with a visible top surface, so no top band reads. The sparse snow flecks on the twigs are scattered highlights, not a horizontal surface. The result is a front elevation of a slender trunk, with no 3/4 volume.

style.evidence: The reference trees have full leafy canopies with 5-6 greens, clumped leaf texture, and a buttressed trunk with roots. The candidate is a thin, sparse bare tree with about 4 grey steps (white, light grey, mid grey, dark, near-black). Its outlines are mostly neutral dark grey/black with little tint, so they lean toward the sticker look. The trunk has birch-like marks, but it is a narrow strip with large areas of one pale tone. The canopy is a sparse scatter of dark pixels with a few snow highlights. Tile density is clearly lower than the references, which are packed with many colours per tile, and the piece reads thinner and flatter next to them.
